programme: NR1H3 (LXRα) and NFKBIB (IκBβ) sit on the two arms of a single lipid-nuclear-receptor / NF-κB inflammatory switch: NR1H3's target set is the canonical LXR lipid-efflux programme (ABCA1, ABCG1, ABCG5, APOE, APOC2, SREBF1, CETP, PLTP) plus TNF, consistent with LXR's known trans-repression of NF-κB-driven cytokine genes; NFKBIB's target set is essentially the NF-κB signalosome and its output (IKBKB, MAP3K14, CHUK feeding TNF, IL1B, PTGS2, NOS2, CXCL8, CCL5, SOD2). DNMT3B sits upstream as an epigenetic gate on the same circuit, sharing the NOS2 node with NFKBIB and reported directly at the TLR4/TNF-α promoter. Together the three read as a myeloid inflammatory-output module (lipid-sensing repression + IκB/NF-κB core + DNA-methylation tuning) converging on TNF/NOS2/IL1B/PTGS2.
role_in_a: In COVID-19 this module maps onto the monocyte/macrophage hyperinflammatory response: TNF, IL1B, NOS2, PTGS2 and CXCL8 (NFKBIB targets) are the core cytokine-storm effectors, and DNMT3B-linked changes at the TLR4/TNF-α promoter have been reported in COVID-19 patients (36840831), consistent with epigenetic loosening of this same inflammatory gate.
role_in_b: In Multiple_sclerosis the same myeloid circuit is expected to operate in microglia/CNS macrophages: NR1H3 carries direct genetic association with MS risk (29801879), and DNMT3B carries an independent MS risk polymorphism (31565203), placing both the lipid-sensing and epigenetic arms of the module in MS separately from any shared study.
shared_axis: Both diseases hinge on myeloid cells — circulating monocytes in COVID-19, resident microglia/macrophages in MS — whose TNF/IL1B/NOS2 output is gated by the same LXR-repression/IκB-NF-κB/DNMT3B-methylation circuit; a disease-specific perturbation of that gate (viral PAMP-driven in COVID-19, risk-allele-driven in MS) would produce myeloid hyperinflammation through the identical downstream genes even though the two diseases arrive at the circuit from different triggers.
reasoning: NR1H3 and DNMT3B are each independently placed in at least one of the two diseases by direct citation, and the module is nameable purely from NFKBIB's and NR1H3's target lists (NF-κB signalosome + cytokines vs. LXR lipid/TNF programme) without needing outside knowledge. But NFKBIB itself — the factor carrying the core NF-κB machinery — has no Open Targets signal or retrieved paper in either disease, and no source ties COVID-19 and MS together through this specific circuit, so the cross-disease link rests on reasoning about shared myeloid biology rather than on anything retrieved jointly.
support: PMID 29801879 — genetic association of NR1H3 with multiple sclerosis risk; PMID 36840831 — altered DNMT3B expression and TLR4/TNF-α promoter methylation in COVID-19; PMID 31565203 — DNMT3B polymorphism associated with multiple sclerosis risk.
how_to_falsify: In matched myeloid populations — COVID-19 blood monocytes and MS microglia/CSF macrophages — knock down or pharmacologically block NFKBIB and test whether NR1H3 agonists still repress TNF/IL1B/NOS2; in parallel, measure DNMT3B-dependent methylation at the TNF/TLR4 promoters in both cell types and correlate with inflammatory gene output and disease severity. If LXR repression of TNF is unchanged when NFKBIB is removed, or promoter methylation state does not track cytokine output, the proposed module does not hold as a shared circuit.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood (COVID-19) vs brain (MS), so this account requires the same myeloid gating circuit to operate in two different compartments (circulating monocyte vs. resident microglia) — plausible for shared myeloid lineage but not demonstrated here. Support fractions are high for the three carrying factors (90, 82, 84 of 104 patient-group comparisons across 6 independent cohort pairs), giving within-study robustness, but this reflects recurrence in the network-inference procedure, not independent experimental replication of the mechanism. Several tissue-generic exclusions (VDR, SREBF1, EZH2, FOXO3, SOX9) are plausible companions to this same lipid/immune axis and were deliberately stripped out — the account should not be extended to lean on them. Single-view exclusions (GFI1, IRF8, TOX2, TFEB, ASXL1, GFI1B) are myeloid/hematopoietic identity factors that might seem to belong in this story but did not recur and are excluded. The remaining concordant factors (ELF3, TFAP2A, MED1, KDM2B, PAX9, E4F1, HMX1, KLF12, BTG2) have epithelial, developmental, or cell-cycle target signatures that do not integrate into this inflammatory module and are deliberately left out of the carrying set.
